Class CausalStreams

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStreams
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class CausalStreams extends Object implements AutoCloseable
The running application: a curated view of the Kafka Streams runtime, assembled by Parsley.streams(Properties) and started here. The surface is an allowlist — each member is present because it is causally inert — and there is no accessor to the underlying KafkaStreams, ever: any single escape hatch would reintroduce the full inherited surface. The withheld members are withheld for different reasons, each with its operational alternative:
  • store() and interactive queries are the causal hazard. The protocol store is internal, and under exactly-once semantics a local store holds the writes of the open transaction until commit or abort, so a query can observe fold state that is not a function of any delivered history. Observe state through sinks.
  • pause()/resume() are a liveness footgun, not a safety hazard. Pausing one instance freezes its release punctuator, and every instance waiting on its outputs stalls with it — a fleet-wide stall commanded from one handle. Stop the instance, or scale by instances.
  • Thread add/remove and cleanUp() are causally inert and withheld only to keep the surface minimal: thread-count changes are scaling, expressed by instances, and cleanup equals deleting the state directory of a stopped instance. A minimal surface can grow compatibly; a regretted member cannot be removed compatibly.

    • setUncaughtExceptionHandler

      public void setUncaughtExceptionHandler(org.apache.kafka.streams.errors.StreamsUncaughtExceptionHandler handler)
      Registers the processing-exception handler. Before start().

      The handler is registered totalized: a handler that throws, or returns null, resolves to SHUTDOWN_CLIENT, with the processing failure and the handler's own failure both logged. Kafka Streams invokes the handler on the failing stream thread with no guard of its own, so a handler failure would otherwise discard the decision, kill the thread without a replacement, and leave the client reporting RUNNING with nothing processing. Shutting down instead keeps handler failure loud.
